Glossary of climate change.fact: global warming controversy Socio-political issues surrounding the theory of global warming.

Glossary of climate change.question: global warming period Any period in which the temperature of the _____'s atmosphere increases
Glossary of climate change.fact: global warming (GW) Usually: the warming trend over the past century or so; also: any period in which the temperature of the Earth's atmosphere increases; also the theory of such changes. global warming period Any period in which the temperature of the Earth's atmosphere increases.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management

Glossary of climate change.fact: hockey stick graph Reconstructions of Northern Hemisphere or global mean temperature changes during the past 600 to 11,300 years, a name coined for the Mann, Bradley and Hughes 1999 (MBH99) reconstruction.

Glossary of climate change.question: Holocene A geological period, which began approximately 11,550 calendar years BP (about 9600 BC) and continued to the _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: Holocene A geological period, which began approximately 11,550 calendar years BP (about 9600 BC) and continued to the Anthropocene.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: ice age A period of long-term reduction in the temperature of _____'s climate, resulting in expansions of continental ice sheets, polar ice sheets, and alpine glaciers
Glossary of climate change.fact: ice age A period of long-term reduction in the temperature of Earth's climate, resulting in expansions of continental ice sheets, polar ice sheets, and alpine glaciers. insolation The amount of solar radiation reaching the surface of the Earth.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: insolation The amount of solar radiation reaching the surface of the _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: ice age A period of long-term reduction in the temperature of Earth's climate, resulting in expansions of continental ice sheets, polar ice sheets, and alpine glaciers. insolation The amount of solar radiation reaching the surface of the Earth.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: IMO In climate change context, It is an acronym for _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: IMO In climate change context, It is an acronym for International Maritime Organization.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: instrumental temperature record _____ the fluctuations of the temperature of the atmosphere and the oceans as measured by temperature sensors
Glossary of climate change.fact: instrumental temperature record Shows the fluctuations of the temperature of the atmosphere and the oceans as measured by temperature sensors.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: The longest-running quasi-global record starts in _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: The longest-running quasi-global record starts in 1850.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO) A cycle of 15 to 30 years between warm or cool waters in the north and south _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO) A cycle of 15 to 30 years between warm or cool waters in the north and south Pacific Ocean.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Members include Japan, the _____, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, Norway, and New Zealand
Glossary of climate change.fact: Members include Japan, the United States, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, Norway, and New Zealand.

Glossary of climate change.question: Iceland, Mexico, and the _____ of Korea may also attend JUSSCANZ meetings
Glossary of climate change.fact: Iceland, Mexico, and the Republic of Korea may also attend JUSSCANZ meetings.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Kyoto Protocol A modification to the _____ on Climate Change
Glossary of climate change.fact: Kyoto Protocol A modification to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: LT-LEDS A long term climate strategy for a country submitted to the _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: LT-LEDS A long term climate strategy for a country submitted to the UNFCCC.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Maunder Minimum A historical period roughly from _____ to 1715, when sunspots became exceedingly rare, as noted by solar observers of the time
Glossary of climate change.fact: Maunder Minimum A historical period roughly from 1645 to 1715, when sunspots became exceedingly rare, as noted by solar observers of the time.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: MSL _____ A historical warm period from about the 10th century to about the 14th century
Glossary of climate change.answer: Mean Sea Level Medieval Warm Period
Glossary of climate change.fact: MSL Mean Sea Level Medieval Warm Period A historical warm period from about the 10th century to about the 14th century.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: NCDS _____ (aka Paris Accord/Agreement) NAPA National Adaptation Programme of Action
Glossary of climate change.fact: NCDS Nationally Determined Contributions (aka Paris Accord/Agreement) NAPA National Adaptation Programme of Action.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: ocean planet The opposite concept of _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: ocean planet The opposite concept of Snowball Earth.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Paleocene–_____ (PETM) A historical warming event which suddenly and fundamentally altered geological and biological aspects of the planet
Glossary of climate change.fact: Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM) A historical warming event which suddenly and fundamentally altered geological and biological aspects of the planet.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: paleoclimatology The study of climate change taken on the scale of the entire history of the _____
Glossary of climate change.fact: ocean planet The opposite concept of Snowball Earth. paleoclimatology The study of climate change taken on the scale of the entire history of the Earth.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Despite its name, polar amplification only applies to the Arctic, and not to the Antarctic, because the _____ acts as a heat sink
Glossary of climate change.fact: Despite its name, polar amplification only applies to the Arctic, and not to the Antarctic, because the Southern Ocean acts as a heat sink.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: regime shift removal unit A tradable carbon credit or "_____ unit" representing an allowance to emit one tonne of greenhouse gases absorbed by a removal or carbon sink activity in an Annex I country
Glossary of climate change.fact: regime shift removal unit A tradable carbon credit or "Kyoto unit" representing an allowance to emit one tonne of greenhouse gases absorbed by a removal or carbon sink activity in an Annex I country.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Snowball Earth solar variation _____ in the amount of radiant energy emitted by the Sun
Glossary of climate change.fact: Snowball Earth solar variation Changes in the amount of radiant energy emitted by the Sun.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: stranded asset _____ that have suffered from unanticipated or premature write-downs, devaluations, or conversion to liabilities
Glossary of climate change.fact: stranded asset Assets that have suffered from unanticipated or premature write-downs, devaluations, or conversion to liabilities.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: TEX-86 A paleothermometer based on the composition of membrane lipids of the marine picoplankton _____ (formerly called Crenarchaeota)
Glossary of climate change.fact: TEX-86 A paleothermometer based on the composition of membrane lipids of the marine picoplankton Thermoproteota (formerly called Crenarchaeota).

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: tipping points in the climate system _____ in the climate system that, when exceeded, can lead to large changes in the state of the system that are often irreversible
Glossary of climate change.fact: tipping points in the climate system Thresholds in the climate system that, when exceeded, can lead to large changes in the state of the system that are often irreversible.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: Water vapor is considered a greenhouse gas because its presence in the _____'s atmosphere contributes to the greenhouse effect
Glossary of climate change.fact: Water vapor is considered a greenhouse gas because its presence in the Earth's atmosphere contributes to the greenhouse effect.

Glossary of climate change.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of climate change.question: hockey stick graph _____ of Northern Hemisphere or global mean temperature changes during the past 600 to 11,300 years, a name coined for the Mann, Bradley and Hughes 1999 (MBH99) reconstruction
Glossary of climate change.fact: hockey stick graph Reconstructions of Northern Hemisphere or global mean temperature changes during the past 600 to 11,300 years, a name coined for the Mann, Bradley and Hughes 1999 (MBH99) reconstruction.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: adductor fossa The adductor fossa or _____ orifice in reptiles and dinosaurs is the major opening into the lower jaw, located between the tooth-bearing region and the jaw articulation
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: adductor fossa The adductor fossa or Meckelian orifice in reptiles and dinosaurs is the major opening into the lower jaw, located between the tooth-bearing region and the jaw articulation. The floor of the opening is formed by the angular and houses the posterior part of the Meckelian cartilage.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The floor of the opening is formed by the angular and houses the posterior part of the _____ cartilage
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: adductor fossa The adductor fossa or Meckelian orifice in reptiles and dinosaurs is the major opening into the lower jaw, located between the tooth-bearing region and the jaw articulation. The floor of the opening is formed by the angular and houses the posterior part of the Meckelian cartilage.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: alveoli _____ alveoli (singular: alveolus) or tooth sockets are pits in the jaws containing the roots of teeth
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: alveoli Dental alveoli (singular: alveolus) or tooth sockets are pits in the jaws containing the roots of teeth.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The condition of having deep alveoli is known as thecodont, and is present throughout _____, including dinosaurs
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: The condition of having deep alveoli is called thecodont, and is present throughout Archosauria, including dinosaurs.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The thecodont condition was historically used to define a clade, the _____, which is now considered paraphyletic and thus obsolete
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: The thecodont condition was historically used to define a clade, the Thecodontia, which is now considered paraphyletic and thus obsolete.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: It forms the floor of the adductor fossa and supports the posterior portion of the _____ cartilage
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: It forms the floor of the adductor fossa and supports the posterior portion of the Meckelian cartilage.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Present in most early _____ (including Archosauria), it is primitively present in dinosaurs; it tends to be large in saurischians, but is reduced or entirely closed in ornithischians
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Present in most early Archosauriformes (including Archosauria), it is primitively present in dinosaurs; it tends to be large in saurischians, but is reduced or entirely closed in ornithischians.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: It is the only endochondral bone of the lower jaw, forming directly out of the posterior part of the _____ cartilage
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: It is the only endochondral bone of the lower jaw, forming directly out of the posterior part of the Meckelian cartilage.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: This condition is found in some derived theropods, including ornithomimids, tyrannosaurids, troodontids, elmisaurids, and _____, and was hypothesized to function as a shock absorber during running, allowing for higher degrees of cursoriality
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: This condition is found in some derived theropods, including ornithomimids, tyrannosaurids, troodontids, elmisaurids, and avimimids, and was hypothesized to function as a shock absorber during running, allowing for higher degrees of cursoriality.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Originally, this character was used to define a clade, the _____, which is now considered polyphyletic
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: arctometatarsal In the arctometatarsalian condition (from Latin arctus – "compressed"), the middle (third) metatarsal of the foot is pinched between the surrounding metatarsals (the second and fourth) at its upper end, thus disappearing in anterior view. Originally, this character was used to define a clade, the Arctometatarsalia, which is now considered polyphyletic.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: bone _____ are, besides teeth, the most common dinosaur body fossils
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: bone Bones are, besides teeth, the most common dinosaur body fossils. Composed of hydroxylapatite, bones are hard mineralized and thus durable.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: There are two principal types of bones: _____ bone is directly formed in the dermis (skin), usually growing from initially thin plates
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: There are two principal types of bones: Dermal bone is directly formed in the dermis (skin), usually growing from initially thin plates. Among others, most bones forming the outer surface of the skull and lower jaws are dermal bones.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: caputegulum _____ (Latin "skull tiles") are flat bones covering the skull bones of ankylosaurs
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: caputegulum Caputegulae (Latin "skull tiles") are flat bones covering the skull bones of ankylosaurs. The position of a caputegulum on the skull can be specified with the use of modifiers; e.g., the nasal caputegulae sit atop the nasal bones.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Coined by William T. Blowes in _____, the term can be used for elements representing both co-ossified osteoderms or cranial sculpturing
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Coined by William T. Blowes in 2001, the term can be used for elements representing both co-ossified osteoderms or cranial sculpturing.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The carpus is especially well ossified in basal ornithischian _____, where it consisted of nine elements
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: The carpus is especially well ossified in basal ornithischian Heterodontosaurus, where it consisted of nine elements.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: caudals The caudals (from _____ caudum — tail), or caudal vertebrae, are the vertebrae that make up the tail
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: caudals The caudals (from Latin caudum — tail), or caudal vertebrae, are the vertebrae that make up the tail.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: caudofemoralis The caudofemoralis muscles, or _____ caudofemoralis, are the main locomotory muscles in all long-tailed dinosaurs
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: caudofemoralis The caudofemoralis muscles, or Musculus caudofemoralis, are the main locomotory muscles in all long-tailed dinosaurs. In long-tailed dinosaurs, the Musculus caudofemoralis is exceptionally large, and can be estimated at 58% of the total mass of the tail in Tyrannosaurus.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: In long-tailed dinosaurs, the _____ caudofemoralis is exceptionally large, and can be estimated at 58% of the total mass of the tail in Tyrannosaurus
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: caudofemoralis The caudofemoralis muscles, or Musculus caudofemoralis, are the main locomotory muscles in all long-tailed dinosaurs. In long-tailed dinosaurs, the Musculus caudofemoralis is exceptionally large, and can be estimated at 58% of the total mass of the tail in Tyrannosaurus.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: This part of the brain usually cannot be observed in dinosaur fossils as it is rarely seen on endocasts; an exception is the possible preservation of cerebellar folia in _____
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: This part of the brain usually cannot be observed in dinosaur fossils as it is rarely seen on endocasts; an exception is the possible preservation of cerebellar folia in Conchoraptor.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Cervical half-rings are a synapomorphy of _____
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Cervical half-rings are a synapomorphy of Ankylosauria.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Some sauropodomorphs, especially some long-necked sauropods such as _____, possessed hyperelongated cervical ribs with posterior processes overlapping two or three preceding vertebrae
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Some sauropodomorphs, especially some long-necked sauropods such as Giraffatitan, possessed hyperelongated cervical ribs with posterior processes overlapping two or three preceding vertebrae.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: chevron _____, or haemal arches, are bones attached to the underside of caudal vertebrae, forming the ventral surface of the tail
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: chevron Chevrons, or haemal arches, are bones attached to the underside of caudal vertebrae, forming the ventral surface of the tail. The openings of multiple consecutive chevrons form the haemal canal of the tail, which protects nerves and blood vessels.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: (see _____ here) cranial kinesis Cranial kinesis is the ability of parts of the skull to move against each other at joints within the skull
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: (see Figure here) cranial kinesis Cranial kinesis is the ability of parts of the skull to move against each other at joints within the skull.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Though cranial kinesis had been proposed for a number of non-avian dinosaur taxa, a _____ review found most of these inferences problematic
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Though cranial kinesis had been proposed for a number of non-avian dinosaur taxa, a 2008 review found most of these inferences problematic.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Different possible causes are debated, and include opisthotonus (death throes) and the release of the _____ elasticum interlaminare during decomposition
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Different possible causes are debated, and include opisthotonus (death throes) and the release of the Ligamentum elasticum interlaminare during decomposition.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: They are identified with _____ numerals from I–V, with I denoting the innermost and V the outermost digit
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: They are identified with Roman numerals from I–V, with I denoting the innermost and V the outermost digit.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Coined by _____ in 2001, the term can be used for elements representing both co-ossified osteoderms or cranial sculpturing
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Coined by William T. Blowes in 2001, the term can be used for elements representing both co-ossified osteoderms or cranial sculpturing.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: They are identified with _____ numerals from I–V, with metacarpal I the innermost (connecting to the thumb) and metacarpal V the outermost
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: They are identified with Roman numerals from I–V, with I denoting the innermost and V the outermost digit.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Together with the lung, air sacs form a highly efficient respiratory system, which in birds is capable of extracting up to _____ more oxygen than is possible in mammals
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Together with the lung, air sacs form a highly efficient respiratory system, which in birds is capable of extracting up to 160% more oxygen than is possible in mammals.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: In long-tailed dinosaurs, the Musculus caudofemoralis is exceptionally large, and can be estimated at _____ of the total mass of the tail in Tyrannosaurus
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: In long-tailed dinosaurs, the Musculus caudofemoralis is exceptionally large, and can be estimated at 58% of the total mass of the tail in Tyrannosaurus.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: In dinosaurs, the crest measures 30–_____ of the length of the humerus
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: In dinosaurs, the crest measures 30–40% of the length of the humerus.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The brachyiliac type is typical for basal sauropodomorph dinosaurs of the _____, while the dolichoiliac type is characteristic of theropods
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: The brachyiliac type is typical for basal sauropodomorph dinosaurs of the Triassic, while the dolichoiliac type is characteristic of theropods.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Both terms were introduced by Edwin Colbert in _____
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Both terms were introduced by Edwin Colbert in 1964.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: endocast _____ are infillings (moulds) of neural cavities, including the braincase and the neural canal of the vertebrae
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: endocast Endocasts are infillings (moulds) of neural cavities, including the braincase and the neural canal of the vertebrae. Endocasts are not exact copies of neural structures though, as neural cavities typically contain additional tissue that may obscure the morphology of the neural structure.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: In Arrhinoceratops and _____, the epijugal forms a distinct jugal horn
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: In Arrhinoceratops and Pentaceratops, the epijugal forms a distinct jugal horn.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The bone can be found in _____ and all ceratopsians more derived than the latter
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: The bone can be found in Yamaceratops and all ceratopsians more derived than the latter.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: epoccipital _____ are dermal ossifications lining the edges of the frills of ceratopsians
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: epoccipital Epoccipitals are dermal ossifications lining the edges of the frills of ceratopsians. Epoccipitals are distinct bones in juveniles but in adults fuse to either the squamosal or parietal, depending on their position.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: epipophysis _____ are bony projections of the cervical vertebrae found in dinosaurs and some fossil basal birds
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: epipophysis Epipophyses are bony projections of the cervical vertebrae found in dinosaurs and some fossil basal birds. Epipophyses provided large attachment areas for several neck muscles; large epipophyses are therefore indicative of a strong neck musculature.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: This is a synapomorphy of _____
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: This is a synapomorphy of Dinosauria.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: horn _____ are outgrowths of skull bones covered by a keratinous sheath
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: horn Horns are outgrowths of skull bones covered by a keratinous sheath.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Other cranial outgrowths or rugosities may be covered by skin structures, as has been proposed for, e.g., the nasal boss of _____ and the domes of pachycephalosaurians
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Other cranial outgrowths or rugosities may be covered by skin structures, as has been proposed for, e.g., the nasal boss of Pachyrhinosaurus and the domes of pachycephalosaurians.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: hyoid _____ are bones of the throat region below and behind the skull that supported the tongue
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: hyoid Hyoids are bones of the throat region below and behind the skull that supported the tongue.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: intercentrum _____ are part of the vertebral column found between centra in the cervical region of some dinosaurs
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: intercentrum Intercentra are part of the vertebral column found between centra in the cervical region of some dinosaurs.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: A primitive feature in tetrapods, interclavicles are generally assumed to be absent in dinosaurs, having been lost in _____
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: A primitive feature in tetrapods, interclavicles are generally assumed to be absent in dinosaurs, having been lost in Dinosauriformes.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: laminae _____ laminae (singular: lamina) or osseous septa (singular: osseus septum) are ridges on vertebrae that divide pneumatic chambers
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: laminae Vertebral laminae (singular: lamina) or osseous septa (singular: osseus septum) are ridges on vertebrae that divide pneumatic chambers.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Example laminae: _____ lamina (SPRL): lamina extending from the neural spine (spino-) to the prezygapophysis (-prezygapophyseal)
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Example laminae: Spinoprezygapophyseal lamina (SPRL): lamina extending from the neural spine (spino-) to the prezygapophysis (-prezygapophyseal).

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Prespinal lamina (_____): lamina extending along the front surface (pre-) of the neural spine (-spinal)
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Prespinal lamina (PRSL): lamina extending along the front surface (pre-) of the neural spine (-spinal).

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina (_____): lamina extending from the posterior end (Posterior) of the centrum (centro-) to the diapophysis (-diapophyseal)
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Posterior centrodiapophyseal lamina (PCDL): lamina extending from the posterior end (Posterior) of the centrum (centro-) to the diapophysis (-diapophyseal).

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Intrapostzygapophyseal lamina (_____): lamina extending between (intra-) the postzygapophyses (-postzygapophyseal)
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Intrapostzygapophyseal lamina (TPOL): lamina extending between (intra-) the postzygapophyses (-postzygapophyseal).

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: An aberrant terminology was proposed by Günter Wagner and Chi-Hua Chiu in _____
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: An aberrant terminology was proposed by Günter Wagner and Chi-Hua Chiu in 2001.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Each half of the mandible, termed a mandibular ramus (plural: mandibular rami; from _____ "branch") or hemimandible, is connected to the quadrate at the back of the skull to form the jaw joint
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Each half of the mandible, termed a mandibular ramus (plural: mandibular rami; from Latin "branch") or hemimandible, is connected to the quadrate at the back of the skull to form the jaw joint.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: The mandible consists of both endochondral bones, which ossified from the _____ cartilage, and dermal bones
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: The mandible consists of both endochondral bones, which ossified from the Meckelian cartilage, and dermal bones.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.question: Meckelian groove _____ groove is a longitudinal channel within the lower jaw
Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.fact: Meckelian groove The Meckelian groove is a longitudinal channel within the lower jaw. It housed the unossified remnants of the Meckelian cartilage (also: Meckel's cartilage), from which the endochondral elements of the lower jaw ossified.

Glossary of dinosaur anatomy.subject: Disaster Management
